Independent hourly ERA5 data

The development API can acquire selected ERA5 point fields, validate their raw files, and save a normalized RDS table without generating EPWs. This workflow requires ERA5 single-level, hourly, explicit ARCO or CDS access. Unsupported routes fail explicitly. It does not generate TMYs or calculate derived variables. The published v0.1.4 workflow remains on legacy; see the migration guide.

Plan before acquiring

library(epwshiftr)
source <- shift_era5(
    2001,
    variables = c("tas", "tdps", "ps", "uas", "vas", "rsds"),
    frequency = "hour",
    access = "arco"
)
site <- shift_site("Singapore", lat = 1.25, lon = 104)
plan <- shift_reanalysis_data(source, site, dry_run = TRUE)
# Equivalently: shift_plan_reanalysis(source, site)
plan$requests[, c("request_id", "variable_id", "expected_hours", "status")]

Planning reads no credentials, writes no files and makes no network requests. These six requests cover 2000-12-31 through 2002-01-01 inclusive: 8,808 hours per field, including a full UTC boundary day on each side. Disjoint year ranges remain separate. Equivalent points and shared raw dependencies are deduplicated; associated site IDs remain in the plan. Request IDs identify the exact dataset and request body. Expected coverage is a request specification, not downloaded coverage. The returned grid coordinates must still be checked.

Exact UTC dates and radiation dependencies

Cloud cover (clt) and direct horizontal solar radiation are listed in the official ERA5 ARCO parameter table. Both access = "arco" and explicit access = "cds" support these fields. Public rsdsdiff expands to its two raw dependencies, SSRD and FDIR; the saved data keep both, without calculating diffuse radiation. The CDS route requires explicit native 0.25-degree coordinates; the following example uses that route.

source <- shift_era5(2001, variables = c("rsdsdiff", "rlds", "clt", "pr"),
    frequency = "hour", access = "cds")
site <- shift_site("grid", lat = -12.5, lon = 131)
dates <- seq(as.Date("2001-06-29"), as.Date("2001-08-02"), by = "day")
plan <- shift_reanalysis_data(source, site, dates = dates, dry_run = TRUE)

dates specifies exact complete UTC days; it does not add padding. Supply the boundary days needed by local-time interpolation and accumulated interval coverage. Dates must fall within the declared years or their immediate boundary days. With dates = NULL, existing full-year ARCO requests remain unchanged. CDS splits each field by month and contiguous date range, requesting a single explicit grid centre. Date gaps are never filled silently. This does not certify provider availability; actual coordinates, units and full hours still require validation. Clouds use explicit fraction/percent units and must lie in [0,100]%; FDIR has the same preceding-hour accumulation contract as SSRD.

Acquire with an explicit budget

Configure your CDS credentials through ECMWF_DATASTORES_KEY or the existing ~/.ecmwfdatastoresrc / ~/.cdsapirc configuration, and accept the dataset’s terms in your CDS account. Do not put credentials in research scripts. Existing CDSAPI_KEY settings are also supported. Authentication and provider availability are only established during actual access.

# This call performs network access. These limits apply to this six-request plan.
result <- shift_reanalysis_data(
    source, site, dir = "era5-singapore-2001",
    limits = list(
        max_submissions = 6,
        max_file_bytes = 16 * 1024^2,
        max_total_bytes = 128 * 1024^2,
        wait_timeout = 900,
        download_timeout = 180,
        total_timeout = 7200
    )
)
result$status
result$requests
result$diagnostics
result$execution
if (identical(result$status, "complete")) {
    weather <- readRDS(result$data$path)
    attr(weather, "reanalysis_schema")
}

Submissions run serially. Submission and total response-body budgets accumulate across calls in the same directory, including failed attempts and control JSON. Timeouts are seconds. total_timeout bounds this invocation’s transfer stage; use a separate process supervisor to limit total execution including local validation and normalization. Without explicit limits, submission and byte budgets are unlimited; wait/download defaults are 3,600/600 seconds.

Byte counts measure response bodies delivered to the reader, separately from bytes written to assets. The first block crossing a threshold is counted and aborts without being written. Already buffered bytes, HTTP/TLS headers and uploads prevent interpreting this as an exact wire-traffic cap. Limits must be chosen for the actual plan; do not increase them merely to bypass a failure.

Understand the saved files

era5-singapore-2001/
  identity.rds                 exact plan and acquisition origin
  result.rds                   latest execution status and diagnostics
  receipts/<request-id>.rds    individual strict-validation records
  transfer/                   network mode
    transfer.json             jobs, request states and cumulative accounting
    raw/<request-id>.asset    retained provider responses
  raw/                        copied assets in local-replay mode
  normalization.rds           normalized-data identity and descriptor
  normalized-<id>.rds          complete normalized long table

Locks exist while an owner is active. Paths in saved descriptors are absolute; moving a directory does not rewrite them. Retain the original layout for normal resume and archive the files with a hash manifest when sharing evidence.

CDS may return ZIP even when NetCDF was requested. A single top-level NetCDF member is extracted temporarily and validated using the same rules as a bare file. The raw ZIP remains unchanged. Artifacts retain its raw_sha256, plus netcdf_member and netcdf_sha256; the member name is missing for bare NetCDF. Multiple or nested NetCDF members are rejected, rather than silently selecting one. Normalized values and UTC semantics are identical for both containers.

Strict validation checks the complete unique ordered UTC axis, scalar returned grid, units, finite values, physical bounds and consistent coordinates across fields. Normalized data retain raw values/units, hashes and interval semantics. Hourly accumulated radiation uses the preceding hour and converts J/m² to W/m² by dividing by 3,600. Skin temperature (skt) is available explicitly but is not automatically added to a request or treated as building ground temperature.

Only complete exposes result$data; partial and failed have data = NULL. An invalid raw asset remains available with a failure record. The normalized identity includes the schema/conversion version, plan, origin and raw hashes. Reopening verifies raw data and normalized-file integrity. This is an acquisition and local data contract, not evidence of coastal-point suitability, TMY representativeness or building-response validity. All boundary hours and raw dependencies remain in the table; downstream study selection must be explicit.

Resume or replay

# Same source, sites, origin and directory; saved limits are inherited.
result <- shift_reanalysis_data(source, site, dir = "era5-singapore-2001")

# Local replay requires one file for every exact request ID.
files <- setNames(
    file.path("supplied-files", paste0(plan$requests$request_id, ".nc")),
    plan$requests$request_id
)
local <- shift_reanalysis_data(source, site, dir = "era5-local", data = files)

Changed plans or origins require a new directory. resume = FALSE refuses an existing execution. Local replay copies the supplied files; the original paths must remain available on later calls, and their provider origin is unauthenticated.

Completed raw assets are reused only after size/hash verification. Partial downloads restart from the saved job’s refreshed result URL, without byte-range resume. Ambiguous submissions are never automatically repeated. A killed process can leave an in-flight attempt with incomplete byte accounting: recovery records that uncertainty and stops new transfers. Verify the recorded owner has stopped before manually recovering any orphan lock; removing a lock does not resolve an ambiguous job or uncertain accounting. Preserve the ledger and raw evidence for diagnosis. A budget-limited recovery test is distinct from a real process-kill experiment.

Plans may be saved with saveRDS() and restored with readRDS() for separate stages. Request values, types and metadata must remain unchanged. Contract validation ignores only data.table’s process-local allocation pointer and does not modify the supplied plan.

For separate stages, use shift_download_reanalysis(plan, dir, limits = ...) and then shift_read_reanalysis(plan, downloaded$files). Transport status downloaded only certifies completed assets. Reader status validated_local describes strict in-memory validation. The high-level complete status also requires successful persistent publication of the normalized output.
